commenti.body:
Chris Marker is certainly one of a kind and no one really does it like him. The closest I could possibly think of is to look into Wim Wender's doc work. *Tokyo-Ga* and *Notebooks on Cities and Clothes* are good starting points. 

  
You could also look into his Left Bank contemporaries - Alain Resnais and Agnes Vada primarily. Both have done incredible doc work. Vada's *Les Glaneurs* and Resnais *Gurnica* and *Night and Fog* are essential

  
Obviously try *Sans Soleil* if you haven't already, one of the greatest achievements in the history of non-fiction filmmaking. His film on Kurosowa (*AK*) is also great.

If you're looking for absurd, I'd highly recommend Fellini, especially his work from La Dolce Vita to Casanova. Interesting place to start might be Orchestra Rehearsal, a mockumentary that explodes into allegory.

Also worth trying some late period Orson Welles. His documentary F for Fake is like an absurdist deconstruction of the medium, and his post-humously finished film The Other Side of the Wind somehow translates the same insane film grammar to a feature.
Thank you so much! Sans soleil was actually on my list! I’ll definitely have to take a look!
That’s amazing I’ll definitely have to look into Orson Welles thank you!

I consider Quentin Dupieux to be an absurdist (?) filmmaker. My favourites of him are ‘Wrong Cops’, ‘Mandibles’ and ‘Keep and Eye out’. 
It’s very interesting how he can dotate the everyday world with his own set of hilarious rules.
Thank you! I believe I’ve heard of him just never had looked into any of his films before! I’ll definitely check him out!
Deerskin is one of the most fun movies ive seen, highly recommend

Oshima's Death by Hanging is sharp and absurd, though maybe in a vein closer to Dr Strangelove (great double feature) than Lynch

Thom Andersen's Los Angeles Plays Itself is a great, cranky essay film

Alain Resnais, one of Marker's collaborators on Statues Also Die, has some other great essay shorts, including Toute la memoire du monde and Le chant du Styrene, and you may also like his features Last Year at Marienbad, Muriel, and Je t'aime, je t'aime

Mr. Oizo is a fucking film maker??? Mind blown. 

The video for flat beat is now even more impressive. I do blame him for progenating dubstep however.

Check out the brief filmography of Jean Vigo. A propos de nice feels like a precursor to Chris Marker's work. L'atalanta is also a masterful film.

News from Home by Chantal Akerman.

Look up some movies by Jonas Mekas to see if he fits your bill. You can find short films online. His most famous work would be Reminiscences of a Journey to Lithuania.

Someone else mentioned keep diving into Chris Marker. Sans Soleil is my favorite film by him. Also check out Three Cheers for the Whale. He made a documentary on the making of Kurosawa's Ran called A.K.

Lynne Sachs helped to update Chris Marker's Three Cheers for the Whale into English toward the end of his life. She's very much influenced by Marker. Many of her films are free to watch on her website.

In the spirit of Grin without a Cat, I'd also recommend the documentary Waiting for Fidel. It's about a filmmaker going to interview Castro in Cuba, but he never shows up for the interview, so it's just two guys walking around discussing the revolution from two different outsider points of view.


Shuji Terayama is similarly absurdist in a David Lynch way. His most famous works are probably Emperor Tomato Ketchup and Pastoral: To Die in the Country.

Maybe check out Guy Maddin and see if he's up your alley. Start with My Winnipeg, his most famous work. The Green Fog is also absolutely bizarre. It's a retelling of Vertigo, but using clips from all sorts of other movies filmed in San Francisco (including Godzilla).

I think that's everything that's coming to mind right now. Chris Marker also has some excellent photography books.
Oh yeah!!! I completely forgot about Resnais I hadn’t even thought to check his films out I’ll definitely have to!

That’s phenomenal thank you so much! I was completely unaware that Marker had photography books as well! It does honestly make a lot of sense though given what he’s produced in his film career! I’ll definitely have to check those out!

Rule 1 of this sub under "Posts" is: "Threads must promote in-depth discussion." Recommendation requests don't do that, so this post is not fitting for the sub. This should have been asked in the "Casual discussion thread" instead. Having said that, I can recommend Tarkovsky's "Stalker", "The Sacrifice" and "Andrei Rublev", Terence Malick's "The Tree of Life",  Ceylan's "Wild Pear Tree". These recommendations are a little slower and more difficult to digest, but I can also recommend the less slow, and more quirky, "Castaway on the Moon" (also known as "Kim's Island"), "The Kid Detective" and "Babbette's Feast".
Thank you so much for the recommendations! So sorry I should’ve gone thoroughly through the rules before hand next time I’ll go through the casual discussion thread!:)
I just watched Night and Fog and that was an absolutely beautiful film. I genuinely had zero idea that Marker had a hand in so many pieces! Thanks again for the recs

Patricio Guzmán was a close friend of Marker, and their work was in communication with each other, aesthetically and politically. I would highly recommend Nostalgia for the Light (2010) as a starting point, followed by The Pearl Button (2015).
Definitely find Welles film Chimes at Midnight

Don't forget Luis Buñuel!  Especially The Exterminating Angel and Simon of the Desert.

And for surreal realism on a completely different level, look into Adam Curtis. Bitter Lake and  HyperNormalisation.
